Command: Do not show favour to the poor in judgment either
Summary: In judgment, do not favour the poor either: pity for a poor litigant must not bend the verdict any more than respect for a rich one.
Commandment: Do not show favour to the poor in judgment either.
Application: Impartiality cuts both ways. Favouring the poor in court feels merciful, but it is still partiality — and it wrongs the other party while patronising the poor man, whose cause should win on its merits.
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: justice is blind to wealth and poverty alike, so favour shown to the poor in judgment is partiality no less than favour shown to the rich.
